lead: Run a whole mission yourself: launch a crew and their kit from Earth, refuel in orbit, test everything on the Moon, fly to Mars when the planets line up, land, and then keep a small colony alive day by day by making air, water, food and fuel from Mars itself. The numbers come from real missions.
try: In Stage 1, pick Starship-class and Crew of 4, then press Next stage. In Stage 2 press Dock the next tanker until the tanks are full (or press Auto-fill). Play on to Stage 6, press Play, and build an Oxygen plant first.
points: Rockets are mostly fuel: only a few tonnes in every hundred reach orbit. So Mars ships go up with empty tanks and are filled by tanker flights.
Earth and Mars line up for the cheap trip only about every 26 months, and the journey takes about 8 to 9 months. India's Mangalyaan cruised for 298 days.
Each person breathes about 0.84 kg of oxygen a day. On Mars you must make it from the carbon dioxide air, as NASA's MOXIE machine proved, a little at a time.
